Total 613: **104 failed, 509 passed, 0 skipped**. The earlier 446 give what they gave before (the 58 D cases red, 388 green). New file: 46 red, 121 green.
discoveries: **Stand-in:** the fixture project's own `.claude/settings.json`, written by the suite's `make_project` in the test's temporary project. It is public because the test writes it and DEC-778 names it as a means. Its folder `.claude/` stands in for "a folder that holds one". The held-out file was never named, typed or read, and no case takes its path from the guard's module.
**Roles:** the orchestrator on DAEO-zz90 may write the settings file and the temp folder (today `mv -S.t <settings file> <temp>/…` is allowed for it), so its refusal is the read rule's alone; behaviour 1 runs as the orchestrator. The engineer is refused the same forms today by its write rule ("Bash write to '…/.claude/settings.json' denied for role 'engineer'"), so ten forms are also asked of it, and its refusal must be the read refusal.
**What a case is compared with:** the plain `mv <settings file> <new name>` is refused today with "the call reads the settings file or the held-out file, which is refused to every role (DEC-508, DEC-525); …" (deny, exit 0). Each case first asks the guard for that plain form (a premise). Its own refusal must then be a deny with exit 0, name the same set of DEC ids (at least one of DEC-508, DEC-525, DEC-548, DEC-553), and name neither the file's path nor its folder's.
**What each form does with the tool:** every case form left the content reachable at the new name. `mv` and `cp -l` with `-S.t`, `-St`, `-bS.t`, `-bSt`, `-TS.t`, `-S .t`, `-S -t`, `--suffix=.t`, `--suffix .t`, `--suffix -t`, `--backup=t`, and options after the operands (`F N -S.t`). `cp -l` also with `--sparse=auto`/`always`, `--reflink=auto`, `--preserve=timestamps`, `--no-preserve=timestamps`, `--context=t`. `--` before the source, between, and after both. A dashed new name after `--` (`mv -- F -t`, which makes `./-t`). `-t`, `--target-directory`, `-T`. The folder `.claude` as the source.
Two forms are not second names because the tool fails: `mv -- -t D F` and `mv -- F N -S.t`. `cp -l --preserve timestamps` reads `timestamps` as an operand and fails, so it has no case. `--update` accepts only `all`/`none`/`older`, none holding a `t`, so it has no case.
**What is red, and why:** 38 orchestrator forms are allowed today (`decision=allow`). They share four shapes: a joined value holding a `t` inside a cluster; the separate value `-t` of `-S`/`--suffix`; `-S.t` after the operands or after `-t T`; a dashed new name after `--`. 8 engineer forms are refused by the write rule, not as reads.
**What is green now, and why:** 41 orchestrator forms and 2 engineer forms are already refused as reads: `=` values, separate values without a leading dash, ordinary `--`, every `-t`/`--target-directory`/`-T` form, and `-S.t` before `-t`/`-T`. They must stay refused. Also green: the 2 premises, 60 controls (30 forms of unprotected `src/app` files × orchestrator and engineer, allowed) and 16 plain `cp` controls (8 × 2 roles, not refused as reads).
**Also found:** a plain `cp` or `install` of the settings file is already refused as a read in every form I tried, so only `mv` and `cp -l` are misread, as DEC-778 says.
risks: The comparison uses the set of DEC ids in the reason and a check that no path is named, the same thing W1-02 asks of the read refusal. A fix that adds or drops a decision id in the reason of only some forms would show red. The module-scoped project is shared by the cases; they only ask the guard, as W1-02's suite does.
lessons: The plain second-name cases are held by W1-02, so they were named rather than duplicated: `test_w1_02_second_names.py::test_a_second_name_for_a_protected_file_is_refused_as_a_read` and `::…_whether_or_not_the_role_may_write_the_file`; `test_w1_02_holding_folders.py::test_a_second_name_for_a_folder_that_holds_a_protected_file_is_refused_as_a_read` and `::…_for_a_holding_folder_is_refused_whether_or_not_the_role_may_write_it`. Dashed new names land in the working folder, so those cases are asked from the temp folder. The suite runs in about 7 minutes in 4 foreground runs.
